The hub.patch.create event metadata gains branch_resolution.

tasks.title: Replace the boolean branch-check hook with a resolver hook and map its errors in the registration handlers
steps: Write TS-21-7, 18, 22, 31, 32, 33, 34 and 37 in internal/workspace (name functions TestTS21_<n>_...) using stub hooks and confirm they fail; the recording stub for TS-21-22 logs call order and a stub insert timestamp

In internal/workspace/branch_check_hook.go delete BranchCheckFunc and define `type BranchResolverFunc func(ctx context.Context, slug, branchName string) (string, error)`; the string result is the resolution method, with exported constants ResolutionLocal="local", ResolutionOriginTracking="origin_tracking", ResolutionOriginFetch="origin_fetch", ResolutionSkipped="skipped". Keep `RegisterBranchCheckHook(fn BranchResolverFunc)` and the package var, still optional/nil-able

Define the error classification without importing carrypatch: an exported interface `BranchResolveError interface{ error; BranchResolveKind() string }` with kind constants not_found, origin_fetch_failed, origin_credentials, workspace_busy, plus an exported constructor NewBranchResolveError(kind string, cause error) error for tests and stubs; the handler classifies with errors.As on that interface so carrypatch can implement the same one-method interface with its own type and no workspace import; any other error (or unknown kind) is the internal class

Add one helper in patch_handlers.go that maps a hook error to a response: not_found -> 400 `branch does not exist in repository or on origin`; origin_fetch_failed -> 502 message `origin fetch failed` with apikit.WriteAPIErrorWithType type `origin_fetch_failed`; origin_credentials -> 502 `failed to resolve origin credentials`; workspace_busy -> 409 type `workspace_busy` message `another operation is running on this workspace; retry later`; anything else -> log slog.Error with slug, branch and error text, then 500 `internal server error`. Never echo the cause text. In a batch only the 400 message gets the `patch[i]: ` prefix

In handleAddPatchSingle call the hook as hook(c.Request().Context(), slug, branch) only when hook != nil and skip_branch_check is not true; capture the returned method; use ResolutionSkipped when skipped and a hook is registered; leave the method empty (key omitted) when no hook is registered. Add `branch_resolution` to the hub.patch.create Metadata next to branch_name and position only when non-empty. Resolution stays before the exists / if_not_exists checks; an if_not_exists hit still emits no event

In handleAddPatchBatch keep the per-element validation loop and call the hook inside it in array order for non-skipped elements only (skipped elements never reach the hook); the first failing element stops the loop and no row is inserted; the duplicate-in-batch and already-registered checks stay after the loop; emit no audit events in the batch path

Update the four existing stubs in internal/workspace/carry_patch_patches_test.go (lines ~712, 753, 784 and any other `func(_, _ string) error`) to the new signature (ctx, slug, branch) (string, error); RegisterBranchCheckHook(nil) cleanups stay as they are

Keep expected 400 text of existing tests in step with the new message `branch does not exist in repository or on origin` (grep internal/ and cmd/ for the old string `branch does not exist in repository`)

tasks.title: Implement the carrypatch branch resolver for local and tracking refs with a locked compare-and-swap create
steps: Write TS-21-1, 2, 4, 8, 9 and 26 in internal/carrypatch (name TestTS21_<n>_...) with real git repositories (bare fork, clone as trunk) via the existing testhelpers_test.go helpers, a recording GitRunner wrapper around carrypatch.NewGitRunnerFactory(), counting fetch and credential stubs and a lock hook; confirm they fail. TS-21-9 is a property test over generated valid branch names and commit chains

Create internal/carrypatch/branch_resolver.go with `NewBranchResolverHook(newRunner func(string)(GitRunner,error), workspaceRoot string, getVariable GetVariableFunc, resolveAuth ResolveAuthFunc, fetch SingleBranchFetchFunc) func(ctx context.Context, slug, branch string) (string, error)`; define `SingleBranchFetchFunc func(ctx context.Context, repoPath, branch string, auth transport.AuthMethod) error`. Do not import internal/workspace. Add an unexported test seam for the lock function (default wslock.TryLock) so TS-21-26 can inject a lock that creates the ref while acquiring

Define a carrypatch error type implementing `BranchResolveKind() string` (kinds not_found, origin_fetch_failed, origin_credentials, workspace_busy, mirrored literally from the workspace package) and a Method string result using the literals local, origin_tracking, origin_fetch

Read PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE once per hook call through getVariable('workspace', slug, 'PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE') using the parse helper that 20_fork_patch_sync added (search internal/carrypatch for it; do not re-implement the rules). If 20's helper is not present yet, add a single exported helper per 20's rules (exact, case-sensitive `origin`, anything else/unset/error means hub) in the file 20 will use and let 20 reuse it

Step 1: resolve `refs/heads/<name>^{commit}` through the runner (git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options); on success return `local` without locking, fetching or writing. Never pass a bare name for existence checks, so tags, SHAs and origin/x are not found

Step 2: if step 1 fails, take the lock with TryLock(slug) (busy -> workspace_busy error, never wait; `defer unlock()` so every outcome releases it); re-check step 1 under the lock and return `local` with no write if it now resolves; then resolve `refs/remotes/origin/<name>^{commit}`; if found, run exactly `update-ref refs/heads/<name> <sha> 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` and return `origin_tracking`. Never use checkout, branch, reset or switch and never write branch.<name>.* config

If the CAS update-ref fails because the ref now exists (detect by re-resolving refs/heads/<name>^{commit}, not by error text), rerun resolution from step 1 once and return `local`; any other update-ref failure returns a plain (unclassified) error wrapped with slug and branch context so the handler answers 500

If the tracking ref is missing: in hub mode return the not_found error and never call fetch or resolveAuth; in origin mode leave a clearly marked branch that returns not_found for now (task 4 fills in the fork fetch) and that passes TS-21-4 unchanged
Add a SingleBranchFetchFunc-based field only through the constructor; confirm with `go build ./...` that nothing in carrypatch imports internal/workspace

tasks.title: Add the single-branch fork fetch step with typed not-found classification
steps: Write TS-21-3 (real bare fork, branch pushed after the clone, real fetch function), TS-21-12 (recording fetch stub), TS-21-13 (stub returning git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate, with and without the tracking ref present) and TS-21-25 (lock spy; fetch and update-ref observe the lock held) and confirm they fail

Implement `DefaultSingleBranchFetch()` in internal/carrypatch/wire.go modelled on upstream.Fetch: git.PlainOpen(repoPath), repo.Remote("origin"), remote.FetchContext with FetchOptions{RemoteName:"origin", RefSpecs: []config.RefSpec{config.RefSpec("+refs/heads/<name>:refs/remotes/origin/<name>")}, Auth: auth, Tags: git.NoTags} and no Prune; treat git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate as success

Verify the unverified go-git behaviour with a real bare fork lacking the branch: capture which error FetchContext returns (expected git.NoMatchingRefSpecError, matched with errors.As). If it is not distinguishable by type from a transport/auth error, instead list the remote (remote.ListContext) and decide not-found from the absence of refs/heads/<name>; never decide from error text alone. Return a typed sentinel (e.g. errBranchNotOnOrigin) from the fetch function for the not-found case

In branch_resolver.go origin mode, under the already-held lock and after the step 1 re-check and tracking check: call resolveAuth(slug) once (error -> origin_credentials error, no fetch), then fetch(ctx, trunkPath, name, auth); NoErrAlreadyUpToDate is success; the typed not-found error -> not_found; any other error -> origin_fetch_failed error that carries the cause for logging; log the cause with slog (slug, branch) and never put it in the message

After a successful fetch re-resolve refs/remotes/origin/<name>^{commit}; if absent return not_found (not a fetch failure); if present create refs/heads/<name> with the same CAS update-ref and return `origin_fetch`, with the same ref-exists-race handling as the tracking path

Assert in TS-21-3 that no other tracking ref and no tag appeared, and in TS-21-12 that the stub receives exactly one refspec, the resolver's auth value, and that resolveAuth was called once with the slug

Also write the classification unit part of TS-21-14 (a fetch error wrapped around the typed error with a misleading message classifies as not found; a plain error with text `couldn't find remote ref` does not) and keep it in the test file for task 5 to complete
